Concept-first rule: one linear equation, light enough. The explainer teaches the seesaw first and the equation second.

routing: Needs a route: the view opens from data-go="mixture"; its four sliders need a state reader; volumes step by 20, so the 20 L and 15 L pours are set as 80 and 60. The skill page opens with a Try first question on a 5-minute clock that can be skipped, and the page also holds a timed simulator elsewhere; the visual itself is untimed.

served.stem: A solution that is 25% acid by volume is mixed with a solution that is 60% acid. To produce 35 liters of a final solution that is 40% acid, how many liters of the 25% solution must be used?

answer.line: 20 L of 25% and 15 L of 60% hold 5 + 9 = 14 L of acid, which is 40% of 35 L.

steps: Picture a seesaw first. 40 sits 15 above 25 and 20 below 60, so the mix leans toward the 25% side: more than half is the 25% solution.
Set the amounts: x liters of 25%, and the rest of the 35 liters at 60%. Track only the acid: 0.25x + 0.60(35 - x) = 0.40(35) = 14.
Check it: 20 L of 25% holds 5 L of acid and 15 L of 60% holds 9 L. 14 L in 35 L is 40%.

choices.note: No single slip lands on 12. With 12 L of the 25% solution the mix comes out at 48%, above the target.
No single slip lands on 10 either. 10 L of the 25% solution makes a 50% mix: too much of the strong one.
25 L likely reuses the 25 from 25%. It would make a 35% mix, below the target.
15 L is how much of the 60% solution goes in. The stem asks for the 25% solution, the bigger pour.
The bigger pour, because 40% sits closer to 25%.

student.lockIt: A mix lands between its parts, closer to the bigger pour. Track the solute, not the liquid.

playWith.label: Mixture Setups: set 25% at 80 and 60% at 60 (the same 4 to 3 split) and watch the blend land on 40%

lever.title: The seesaw: the mix leans toward the bigger pour
lever.foot: 20 L x 15 apart = 15 L x 20 apart, so the seesaw balances at 40%.
